PT Method Physics + Process Variants

PT uses capillary action to draw a low-viscosity penetrant into surface-breaking discontinuities. Process: (1) Pre-clean — degrease + remove paint/scale per SSPC-SP; (2) Apply penetrant — dwell 5-30 min per AMS 2644 sensitivity level; (3) Remove excess — water spray (Method A), emulsifier + water (Method B/D), solvent-wipe (Method C); (4) Apply developer — dry powder (Form a), wet aqueous (Form b/c), non-aqueous wet (Form d), water-soluble (Form e); (5) Develop + inspect — dwell 10-60 min, inspect under white light (visible PT) or UV-A (FPI, 1000+ µW/cm² at 15"); (6) Post-clean.

AMS 2644 Sensitivity Levels + Reference Panels

AMS 2644 classifies penetrant systems by sensitivity (½ = ultra-low, 1 = low, 2 = medium, 3 = high, 4 = ultra-high). Reference: TAM panels (low-cycle fatigue) + NiCr-plated panels per Pratt & Whitney spec PWA 9610. Atlantis NDT inspectors verify panel sensitivity pre-job + every shift change. Verification logged + Level III signed via Atlantis NDT ERP calibration tracking.

Code + Acceptance Criteria

PT acceptance per: ASME Section V Article 6 (general PT) + Mandatory Appendices; ASTM E1417 standard practice + ASTM E165 standard test method; AMS 2644 sensitivity classification; NAS 410 + EN 4179 aerospace inspector certification; API 570 piping in-service; API 653 storage tank; ASME B&PV Section VIII Div 1/2; AWS D1.1/D1.6 structural; ISO 3452 + ISO 12706 EU penetrant systems. Acceptance: round indications ≤ 3/16" + linear indications per pre-defined L/W ratio criteria per applicable construction code.

PT Limitations + Method Selection

Limitations: surface-breaking ONLY (no subsurface detection); requires clean, smooth surface; sensitive to paint/coating (max ≤ 25 µm DFT typically); temperature 5-50°C operating range typical (extended range with special penetrants); contamination drift on porous materials. Where PT fails: use MT (ferromagnetic surface), ECA (thin-wall conductive), UT (volumetric), RT (volumetric).

PT Frequently Asked Questions

Q1: When is fluorescent PT (FPI) required over visible dye?

A: Aerospace + nuclear + critical-fatigue components per NAS 410 + EN 4179 + ASME XI typically require Type I (FPI) Level 3-4 sensitivity. Visible dye Type II is acceptable for general structural welding per AWS D1.1.

Q2: What temperature range works for PT?

A: Standard penetrants 5-50°C. Cold-weather penetrants below 5°C. Hot-service penetrants up to 175°C (specialised). Outside range — qualify alternate procedure per ASME V Article 6 Mandatory Appendix or use MT/ECA.

Q3: Why is post-cleaning critical?

A: Residual penetrant can contaminate subsequent processes (welding, anodising, painting), reduce corrosion resistance on austenitic SS, and create false-positive findings on later inspections. Per ASTM E1417 §10 + applicable customer specification.

Q4: ASNT cert level for PT?

A: Level II — acquisition + interpretation; Level III — procedure authoring + final disposition. Atlantis Academy 96% first-pass via SNT-TC-1A + ISO 9712 + NAS 410 pathway.
